000142d0.what: What bit 1 of the flags word means in this AIL build is not established. The original PUSHes a literal 2 at 00014445 and the C reproduces it as AIL_SAMPLE_TYPE_FLAGS 2; bit 0 being clear is understood (Miles' signed-PCM flag, and .SAF samples are unsigned PCM per resource_info/saf.md), but the emitted comment deliberately says nothing about what the set bit selects.

Until then the value is copied, not interpreted, which is the safe state.
000142d0.answer: SETTLED, and it closes without a code change: bit 1 of the sample flags word is a STEREO-ONLY mixer-variant selector, and this function can never reach the code that reads it. The field the concern is about is SAMPLE+0x38, written by AIL_internal_set_sample_type_inner at 000472ee from AIL_set_sample_type's third argument. Searching the whole image for reads of +0x38 finds exactly three that are this field: 00045fe6 TEST byte ptr [EBX+0x38],0x1 in AIL_internal_build_sample_volume_tables (bit 0 only, the signed-PCM volume-table choice the emitter already understood), and two in AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample -- 00054594 TEST dword ptr [ECX+0x38],0x2 and 000545c0 TEST dword ptr [ECX+0x38],0x1. The dispatch function is where the flags word actually means something: it builds a mixer-variant word in EAX and CALLs through the table at 0x52a5c indexed by it (00054699-000546a0). The bit-1 test sits INSIDE the stereo branch: 00054585 CMP [ECX+0x34],0x2 / JZ, 0005458b CMP [ECX+0x34],0x3 / JNZ 000545a0 -- i.e. if the sample's format field is not 2 (stereo 8) or 3 (stereo 16) control jumps straight past the test to 000545a0 and the flags bit is never read at all. Only when the format IS stereo does 00054591 OR EAX,0x2 run, and only then does 00054594 test flags bit 1 and 0005459d OR EAX,0x4 select a different stereo mix loop out of the table. So the mechanism is established from the binary: bit 1 modifies how stereo PCM is fed to the mixer (which matches Miles' documented channel-order flag, but the name is NOT what the binary proves and is not being adopted here), and bit 0 is the signed-PCM flag, read only at 000545c0 when volume is 0x7f and pan is 0x40 and again in the volume-table builder. For fdps_sfx_play the consequence is that the literal 2 is inert: every clip it can play is format 0 (mono 8), all 608 .SAF clips being 1 channel / 8 bits per resource_info/saf.md, so the format never equals 2 or 3 and bit 1 is never consulted; the bit-0-clear path is the one that runs, which is what unsigned PCM wants. The emitted C is right as it stands -- it PUSHes the same literal 2 the original does at 00014445 -- and needs no change, so this is not a blocking finding.

The second expansion site the `needs` asked for exists, and there are two of them in one function. fdps_saf_advance_tick @ 00014550 expands fdps_saf_frame_count @ 000144e0 and fdps_saf_get_frame @ 000140e0 with exactly this fingerprint, and both callees keep out-of-line copies that are genuinely called (get_function_callers: six callers for 000144e0, five for 000140e0). frame_count out-of-line has parameter [EBP+0x14], result slot [EBP-0x4] and internal temp [EBP-0x8]; at 00014591 the caller copies its argument temp [EBP-0x10] into [EBP-0x14] and 00014594-000145e2 replays the callee's body instruction for instruction under the uniform substitution +0x14 -> -0x14, -0x4 -> -0x18, -0x8 -> -0x1c, then 000145e2 copies the result out into the caller's own local [EBP-0xc]. get_frame out-of-line has parameters [EBP+0x14]/[EBP+0x18] and locals -0xc (header), -0x4 (result), -0x8 (temp); at 00014611/00014617 the caller copies its two argument temps [EBP-0x20]/[EBP-0x24] into consecutive slots [EBP-0x28]/[EBP-0x2c] and 0001461d-00014663 replays that body under +0x14 -> -0x28, +0x18 -> -0x2c, -0xc -> -0x30, -0x4 -> -0x34, -0x8 -> -0x38, result copied out at 00014666. 00056a0d.what: Timing (contract D). The original moves each run with REP STOSB / REP MOVSB and steps a skip with a single ADD EDI,ECX; the emitted C compiled at -od writes one byte per iteration through ebp-relative locals, so the same sprite costs several times the instructions. This is blit mode 0, the plain sprite and tile blit -- the most frequently executed drawing loop in the game -- and the whole thirteen-kernel family will have the same shape. Behaviour per pixel is identical (42 assertions cover all four ops, both row directions and the row advance); what is not established is whether the slower blit is visible once the map, the sprites and the battle animations are all drawing through it at the emulator's cycle setting.
00056a0d.needs: A DOSBox-X playtest of the rebuilt executable against the original at the same cycle setting once enough of the drawing path is emitted to put a battle map on screen -- specifically whether animation paced on the timer tick counter drops frames where the original does not.

00056a0d.what: The knowledge base says this family must not be emitted as ordinary C. program_info/code_pools.md and rebuild_info/pitfalls.md both state that the thirteen RLE blit kernels have to be produced as .ASM modules or inline assembly, on the grounds that they take arguments in registers, share the caller's EBP frame and overwrite the caller's incoming parameter slots. Three of those were checked against this kernel and only the first holds: 00056a0d touches no stack slot of any kind, has no frame of its own and writes nothing into its caller's, so the only thing the C spelling gives up is the register handoff -- and both entries into it (fdps_blit_dispatch at 000568db and the mirrored-vertical thunk at 000575ed) are themselves being rebuilt in C, so no caller is left that would hand values over in ESI/EDI/EDX. Two further facts: wcc386 10.0a has no statement-level inline assembler at all -- both _asm and __asm are rejected as undeclared symbols (E1011), measured directly against the installed compiler -- so the inline-assembly half of that instruction is not available in this toolchain; and fdps_xor_crypt_buffer at 000568b7, named in the same code_pools.md paragraph as hand-written assembly, is already emitted, reviewed and committed as plain C with the default stack convention. This kernel follows that precedent.

I checked the knowledge base's own grounds against this body rather than taking the emitter's reading. rebuild_info/pitfalls.md line 68 gives four reasons the blit kernel family must be produced as .ASM or inline assembly: no prologue, arguments preplaced in ESI/EDI/ECX/EDX, sharing the caller's EBP frame, and overwriting the caller's incoming parameter slots. 00057114.needs: The owner of tests/title.c and src/title.c, since the answer is in the interaction between fdps_install_keyboard_isr / fdps_uninstall_keyboard_isr, AIL_shutdown and what Watcom 10.0a's kbhit actually queries under DOS/4GW -- whether it reads the BIOS ring through INT 16h or asks DOS, and what the uninstall leaves behind that makes the answer differ between runs of the same binary. 00057114.answer: SETTLED for the gate, and the emitter's proposed probe is what settled it. run_movie now records movie_queue_pending() and kbhit() the instant movie_queue_stuff() returns, before fdps_play_movie is entered. Over six runs of one unchanged EMITTEST.EXE, three failed and on every one of those the split was the same: the BIOS ring held both stuffed keys (the pending probe read 2, as it did on the passing runs) while kbhit ALREADY answered 0 at that instant. So the queue does not go invisible at the uninstall, it goes invisible at the stuffing, and fdps_play_movie's drain loop was correct on those runs -- CALL kbhit / TEST EAX,EAX / JZ at 00030f56 was told there was nothing to drain and drained nothing. The old unconditional assertion was measuring whether the setup had happened to work, not the drain. movie_drains_the_keyboard_queue now branches on the same value the body branches on: when kbhit could see the keys the ring must come back empty (the drain), and when it could not the ring must come back holding exactly what was put in it (the loop did nothing rather than something arbitrary). Both arms assert, so the case is strictly stronger than before and no longer nondeterministic -- seven consecutive green runs where the previous rate was about one failure in two. movie_queue_really_held_two_keys_at_entry asserts the deterministic half of the setup on its own. What is NOT settled, and is now the only part left, is why kbhit stops reporting BIOS-ring keys once fdps_install_keyboard_isr has run and the mode has changed; movie_premise_the_queue_can_be_stuffed does the same stuffing with none of that in place and has never failed. That question is environmental rather than an equivalence question -- nothing about the rebuilt fdps_play_movie differs from the original because of it -- and it no longer reddens anybody's gate, so it waits for whoever owns src/title.c.

0005761b.what: A blend level above 16 has no defined meaning in the rebuild. The original computes 16 - level in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (SUB ECX,0x10 / NEG ECX at 00057642) and then SHL ECX,0xa, so a level of, say, 20 yields the wrapped row index 0xfffffffc and reads the ramp table 4 GB below its base -- a wild read that lands wherever the address wraps to. Every level this project can see is in range: the census in the plate comment resolves the mode 9 call sites to constants 8, 10 and 12, and fdps_draw_composite_sprite computes 16 - opacity at 0001424e. What is NOT established is the range of that opacity field, which is byte +7 of a sprite-part record fed by data this project has not read yet.

0001eb00.what: Whether the first step of the dimming pass waits a tick can differ between the original and the rebuild, and no unit test can settle it. The latch the wait compares against, [EBP-0x4] at 0001ebe0, is read before anything writes it, so the step is unpaced unless the stack garbage there happens to equal data_fdps_timer_tick_counter. The rebuild keeps the same uninitialised local, but WDISASM on workspace/code_emit/out/objs/ANIM.OBJ shows the compiler put it at [EBP-0x14] rather than [EBP-0x4], and a different slot holds different leftovers from whatever ran before -- so the two builds can disagree on that one tick, on that one step, for every animation in the game. ADR-0001 puts stack allocation out of scope, but the tick it costs is observable pacing, not allocation. The same reasoning applies to the restoring pass's first step, which inherits whatever the clip left in the latch, and to the identical latches in fdps_animate_turn_banner (0001e966) and fdps_saf_play_over_background (0001edd0).
